description: NASA Enthusiasts is an individual team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. I am a first-year Instrumentation and Control Engineering student interested in space exploration, astronomy, technology, and interactive application development. I aim to create an engaging and educational Astronaut Mission Trainer app that combines learning, interactive scenarios, and animations. I am excited to explore new ideas, learn, and develop a creative solution.
summary: Moon Outpost Trainer is a text-based game written in C for the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer". The player is the Commander of a Moon outpost and must balance three resources: power, oxygen and food. Each action, such as cleaning solar panels, running the oxygen generator or growing food, improves one resource and costs another. A solar storm, inspired by NASA space weather data, then tests the player's choice. The mission succeeds or fails depending on the remaining resources. The game teaches students that life support decisions on a space mission are connected trade-offs.
details: Moon Outpost Trainer is a text-based game written in C. The player enters a commander name and sees the outpost's power, oxygen and food, each starting at 100. The player chooses one action: clean the solar panels (power +20, food -10), run the oxygen generator (oxygen +20, power -15) or grow food (food +20, power -10). A solar storm then reduces power by 20, inspired by NASA space weather data. If power, oxygen or food reaches 0 the mission fails, otherwise it succeeds. Benefit: students see that life support decisions on a Moon base are connected trade-offs. Tools: C language (variables, printf, scanf, if/else), VS Code. Game values are simplified for gameplay and are not real mission values. In the future we plan multiple days, more events and real NASA data.
dataRefs: NASA DONKI space weather database (inspired the solar storm event)
